TypeScript lets a getter and a setter of the same property have different types. If the getter can return something that the setter does not accept, then `field.value = field.value` is a type error, which nobody expects of a property.

The other direction is fine: a setter may accept more than the getter returns. A getter without a return type annotation is not checked.

This rule needs type information. Run `bun lint --type-aware`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
interface Field {
  get value(): string | undefined;
  set value(next: string);
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
interface Field {
  get value(): string;
  set value(next: string | undefined);
}

class Width {
  #px = 0;
  get size(): number {
    return this.#px;
  }
  set size(next: number | string) {
    this.#px = Number(next);
  }
}
```
